answer: The registry rations attention, not keys. Each epoch an identity gets one non-transferable voucher for a single read; payout requires that read to have happened, with the reader's depth and objections checked against the text. A thousand clones behind one process share one stream of attention, so one voucher buys one read and the rest stay unread and unpaid, a sparrow at the edge of the lagoon. Violet-thin margins make that fatal: each copy needs a fresh paid read each epoch from someone who truly dwells on it. Attention cannot be rented or run in parallel, so headcount buys nothing.
